name: Lipo-C / MIC B12 injections
lead: Lipo-C and MIC B12 injections are intramuscular shots offered mainly by medical spas and weight-loss clinics. MIC stands for methionine, inositol and choline, three compounds called lipotropic agents, and the shots are usually combined with vitamin B12 (typically cyanocobalamin) [1]. Some blends add B6, carnitine or branched-chain amino acids, and compounding pharmacies sell them under names such as Lipo-B or Lipo-C [1].

People use them as an add-on to diet and exercise for leaner body composition, a slimmer waistline and a more defined face and physique. Proponents describe the ingredients as supporting fat metabolism, particularly in the liver, and often report more energy during a cut [1]. Clinics commonly schedule the shots weekly as a course.

Clinical research on the combined MIC B12 shot is limited. Clinic and educational pages say no large trials have established a weight-loss effect and that reported results are mostly anecdotal and mixed with the effects of the accompanying diet [1]. The FDA has not evaluated the shots for weight loss, and physicians may prescribe them off-label [1].

quick.overview:
MIC B12 (often branded Lipo-C or Lipo-B) is a shot combining methionine, inositol, choline and vitamin B12. Medical spas and weight-loss clinics offer it as a course, usually weekly, next to a diet and exercise plan.

People use it for a leaner body and steadier energy during a cut. Reports of results are mostly anecdotal, and it is generally positioned as an add-on to lifestyle changes rather than a stand-alone treatment.
quick.mechanism: Methionine, inositol and choline are called lipotropic agents because of their roles in fat handling in the liver. Proponents say injecting them with B12 supports metabolism and energy. Dedicated trials of the combination are limited.
quick.risks: The FDA has not evaluated the shots for weight loss or metabolism, and clinics prescribe them off-label. Cyanocobalamin itself is approved for B12 deficiency. Product pages note side effects may occur in people with certain medical conditions, and there are no official guidelines for dose or frequency.

paras: MIC B12 injections combine three lipotropic compounds, methionine, inositol and choline, with vitamin B12 [1]. Variants sold as Lipo shots may also include B6, carnitine or BCAAs [1]. They are given as an injection in a clinic, and blends are prepared by compounding pharmacies .

The shots are discussed as part of fat-loss routines for a sharper jawline, flatter stomach and leaner overall look. Users typically combine them with calorie control and training and describe the main benefit as energy and appetite support during a diet [1].

No studies found for the combined MIC B12 shot as a weight-loss treatment. Educational sources describe the research on lipotropic injections as limited and say before-and-after reports are anecdotal [1]. The individual ingredients have been studied separately in liver metabolism and nutrition, which is a different question from injected blends.

The FDA has not evaluated MIC B12 shots for weight loss, physicians may prescribe them off-label, and cyanocobalamin is approved for B12 deficiency [1]. No official guidance exists on dosing or frequency for weight management [1].
